title: Existence of a regular meromorphic section
statement: Let X be a proper locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism] over a field k with finite dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and no embedded points, and let L be an invertible O_X-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then there exists a meromorphic section s of L such that the canonical map K_X \to K_X(L) is injective (that is, s is a regular meromorphic section in the sense of Stacks Project, Divisors, Tag 02OZ).

source.place: Tag 02OZ (Lemma 31.5.10, label divisors-lemma-regular-meromorphic-section-exists), case (3), for a scheme without embedded points

proof.text: Choose a local free generator of L near each point using [def-sc-invertible-module]. Its germ is a free generator of the stalk, by the existing proved private helper AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.stalk_generator_bijective in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.InvertiblePullbackTensor (reused by a proof-only import all). The helper represents coefficients and module elements on smaller neighborhoods, and shrinks an equality of germs before applying uniqueness of the local coefficients [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Apply [lem-sc-meromorphic-sheaf-generic-product]. Its normalized additive stalk identifications are linear: the localization map on stalks is linear and, under these identifications, is the identity (for O_X use the canonical structure-sheaf stalk identification). Hence it is surjective, and linearity transports to the identifications. On every open U, transport the component maps a_eta ↦ a_eta s_eta through the two product bijections to obtain an additive, O_X(U)-linear map F_U: K_X(U) → K_X(L)(U). The germ restriction formulas show that these maps commute with restriction, giving a morphism F of O_X-modules.

source.place: Tag 0EMI, proof: pick a generator s_eta of the free rank 1 module L_eta at each generic point, using the description of K_X and K_X(L) in Tag 0EMH

proof.text: Each F_U is injective: equality of its values implies equality of every generic coefficient, because scalar multiplication by the chosen free generator s_eta is injective; the product bijection for K_X then implies equality of sections. Therefore F is a monomorphism. Set s to be the composite O_X → K_X → K_X(L), using the canonical localization map. The unique extension property in [def-sc-meromorphic-module] identifies meromorphicSectionMap(s) with F, so s is a regular meromorphic section.

source.place: Tag 0EMI, proof: s = prod s_eta is a regular meromorphic section
